stages.title: Advanced linguistics and grammar
stages.hook: Japanese attaches endings to a verb like beads on a string: 食べさせられたくなかった. How does that work?
explain: Linguists describe Japanese as an agglutinative (膠着語, kōchakugo) language: suffixes are strung onto a verb stem in a fixed order, each with one function. 食べ-させ-られ-たく-なかっ-た means "did not want to be made to eat": stem, causative, passive, desiderative, negative, past.

Particles (助詞, joshi) mark grammatical relations, and auxiliary verbs (助動詞, jodōshi) add tense, negation, politeness and modality. The basic order is subject–object–verb, and modifiers precede the noun, including whole clauses: 昨日買った本 (the book I bought yesterday).

The topic marker は and the subject marker が are a famous problem. は marks what the sentence is about (topic), often with contrast, while が marks new or focused information. The unit of timing is the mora (拍, haku), not the syllable, which explains the importance of long vowels and the moraic ん.
stages.mnemonic: Stem + suffix chain: each suffix does one job.
sentences: Particles show relations in a sentence.
The topic and the subject are distinguished.

o: Suffixes are added in a chain to a stem
Words never change, so grammar is by order alone
Only the tone of the voice changes
Words are written without any vowels
gq.why: Suffixes with single functions are added to a stem.

gq.q: What is the timing unit in Japanese?
gq.why: The mora (haku) is the unit of timing.

panel.q: In 食べさせられたくなかった, what does させ contribute?
panel.why: させ is the causative suffix.

panel.q: What does the topic は typically signal?
o: The object of the verb only
The time of the action only
panel.why: は marks what the sentence is about, often with a contrast.

panel.q: How does Japanese place a relative clause?
o: At the end of the sentence
panel.why: Modifier clauses come before the noun.

teach.model: Japanese attaches suffixes in a fixed chain to a verb stem. Particles mark relations, modifiers precede nouns and timing is counted in morae. は marks the topic and が marks new information.

trip.prompt: Segment the chain 食べさせられたくなかった into morphemes.

stages.title: Historical development of the language
stages.hook: Japanese had no writing of its own, so it borrowed characters. How did two kana scripts grow from kanji?
explain: Early Japanese (上代日本語, jōdai Nihongo, Old Japanese) was written using Chinese characters. In the 『万葉集』 (Man'yōshū, 8th century), characters were used for their sounds, called 万葉仮名 (man'yōgana). Hiragana developed from cursive forms of man'yōgana, and katakana from parts of kanji used by scholars and monks as reading aids.

For centuries, formal writing used 漢文 (kanbun, Classical Chinese), read in Japanese order by 訓読 (kundoku). Classical Japanese (古文, kobun) differs from modern grammar in verb endings and particles. Heian literature, such as the Tale of Genji, was written mostly in hiragana.

In the Meiji period, the 言文一致 (genbun itchi) movement brought the written language closer to speech. In 1946, 現代仮名遣い (modern kana usage) reformed spelling, and the set of commonly used kanji was limited. Sound changes also happened: for example, an old p sound became f and then h.
stages.mnemonic: Kanji for sound, kana from kanji.
items: unification of spoken and written style
sentences: The genbun itchi movement began in the Meiji era.
Classical Japanese has different grammar from modern.

o: Oracle bones from the Shang dynasty
gq.why: Hiragana came from cursive forms of man'yōgana.

o: A kind of poetry from the Heian period
A dictionary of old kanji readings
gq.why: It aimed to bring written style closer to spoken style.

panel.q: Why were characters used for sound in the Man'yōshū?
o: Because it was a Chinese book
panel.why: Japanese had no writing, so Chinese characters were used phonetically as well as for meaning.

panel.q: What did katakana originate as?
o: Parts of kanji used by scholars
Cursive forms of whole kanji used by court ladies
A loan from the Korean script
panel.why: Katakana came from parts of kanji used as reading aids.

panel.q: Why can Heian texts feel different to modern readers?
panel.why: Classical grammar and vocabulary differ from modern Japanese.

teach.model: Japanese borrowed Chinese characters and used them for sound as man'yōgana. Hiragana came from cursive forms and katakana from kanji parts. Genbun itchi in the Meiji period brought writing closer to speech.

points.ask: Where did the writing come from?
What happened in the Meiji era?

trip.prompt: Look at an image of man'yōgana and compare it with a hiragana chart.

stages.title: Literature and cultural discourse
stages.hook: "In spring, the dawn." These three words open a famous Heian essay. What makes classical Japanese writing so concise?
explain: 『枕草子』 (The Pillow Book), by 清少納言 (Sei Shōnagon), is a Heian-period collection of essays that begins 春はあけぼの ("In spring, the dawn"). It is an example of 随筆 (zuihitsu), loosely connected writing. The aesthetic ideas of もののあわれ (mono no aware, the pathos of things) and 侘び寂び (wabi-sabi, beauty in simplicity and imperfection) shape Japanese cultural discourse.

The scholar 本居宣長 (Motoori Norinaga) used もののあわれ to interpret The Tale of Genji. In the modern period, the 私小説 (shishōsetsu, I-novel) shaped confessional fiction. 川端康成 (Kawabata Yasunari) won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1968, and 大江健三郎 (Ōe Kenzaburō) in 1994.

Cultural terms like wabi-sabi are often simplified abroad. Scholars debate how old and how uniform such ideas are and how they were shaped by modern nationalism and tourism. A critical reader asks who is using a concept and for what purpose.
stages.mnemonic: Short, seasonal, suggestive: a classical style.
sentences: Motoori Norinaga discussed mono no aware.
Kawabata Yasunari received the Nobel Prize.

gq.why: Sei Shōnagon wrote the Pillow Book.

gq.q: Which writer won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1968?

panel.q: What is 随筆?
o: A court poem in thirty-one sounds
A long novel about court life
panel.why: It is a loosely connected essay form.

panel.q: Why should a critical reader be cautious about wabi-sabi explanations?
o: They are always exact and complete
They have no history at all
panel.why: Concepts are simplified and shaped by history and use.

panel.q: What did Motoori Norinaga use mono no aware for?
o: To write haiku in the Edo period
To interpret the Tale of Genji
To translate the Bible into Japanese
panel.why: He used it to interpret The Tale of Genji.

teach.model: The Pillow Book is a Heian essay collection. Ideas like mono no aware and wabi-sabi shape cultural discourse, but scholars note they are simplified and historically shaped. Japanese writers won Nobel Prizes in 1968 and 1994.

trip.prompt: Read the opening section of The Pillow Book in translation and note one season image.

stages.title: Advanced academic writing
stages.hook: What does a Japanese research paper include before the main text? An abstract and keywords, then a careful structure.
explain: A Japanese research article normally has a title, 要旨 (yōshi, abstract), キーワード (keywords), 序論 (introduction), 先行研究 (previous research), 研究方法 (kenkyū hōhō, methods), 結果 (results), 考察 (discussion), 結論 and 参考文献 (sankō bunken, references). 脚注 (kyakuchū) are footnotes.

The purpose statement is typical: 本研究の目的は…を明らかにすることである (the aim of this study is to clarify…). Claims are hedged with 〜と考えられる and 〜の可能性がある. A section on 限界 (genkai, limitations) is expected, such as small sample size.

Peer review (査読, sadoku) checks quality before publication. References follow a consistent style set by the field or journal. Terminology is defined at first use, and abbreviations are explained. Clear logic matters more than ornate writing.
sentences: The aim is to clarify the actual situation.

o: A footnote at the page end

gq.q: What does a 限界 section discuss?
gq.why: It discusses what the study cannot show.

panel.q: Why define terms at first use?
o: Because it is a rule of kanji
panel.why: Readers must know exactly how the term is used.

panel.q: A study with 12 participants claims a national trend. What is the best revision?
o: Remove the references to look confident
State it as a law of the nation
Add more kanji to look scholarly
panel.why: The claim should be hedged and the limitation stated.

panel.q: Which clause fits a purpose statement?
o: 本研究の目的は実態を明らかにすることである
panel.why: The aim is stated with 目的は…明らかにする.

teach.model: A research article has an abstract, keywords, introduction, method, results, discussion, conclusion and references. State the aim, hedge claims, define terms and discuss limitations. Peer review checks quality.

points.ask: How do I state the aim?

trip.prompt: Read about peer review and list one strength and one weakness.

stages.title: Professional translation
stages.hook: Why do translators keep a "memory" of every sentence they have translated? Efficiency and consistency.
explain: Professional translation uses tools. A translation memory (翻訳メモリ, honyaku memori) stores past translated sentences for reuse. A glossary (用語集) keeps terms consistent. Machine translation (機械翻訳) produces drafts, and human post-editing (ポストエディット) corrects them. Delivery date (納期, nōki) and quality control (品質管理, hinshitsu kanri) are part of the job.

Japanese–English translation raises special problems. Subjects are often omitted and must be supplied. Politeness levels must be handled by tone. Katakana loanword spelling needs a standard: コンピューター or コンピュータ, depending on the style guide. Numbers, units and dates need conversion and checking: 令和 (Reiwa) years and the Gregorian calendar.

Localisation (ローカライズ, rōkaraizu) adapts product text, screens, units and cultural references. Machine translation can omit negation or mistake the subject, so check safety-critical text carefully. Confidentiality and client style guides are professional obligations.
sentences: A human checks the machine translation output.
We keep to the deadline and quality.

gq.q: What does a translation memory do?
gq.why: It stores earlier translated segments for reuse.

o: Writing the first draft by hand
gq.why: A human corrects the machine output.

panel.q: Why can machine translation be dangerous in a manual?
o: It may drop a "not" or confuse the subject
panel.why: It can omit negation or mistranslate the subject.

panel.q: What must a translator do with an omitted subject when translating into English?
o: Leave it blank in the English
Ask the printer to add it
panel.why: English usually needs an explicit subject.

panel.q: Why does a style guide fix コンピューター versus コンピュータ?
panel.why: Consistency within a document matters.

teach.model: Translators use translation memories, glossaries and machine translation with post-editing. They supply omitted subjects, control terminology, check numbers and localise content. Safety-critical text needs careful human review.

trip.prompt: Read about translation memory and explain how it saves time.

stages.title: Interpretation of complex communication
stages.hook: A Japanese colleague says 善処します. Does it mean "I will fix it"? The real meaning needs interpretation.
explain: Pragmatics (語用論, goyōron) studies meaning in use. Japanese communication often uses indirect, softened wording (婉曲, enkyoku). 善処します (I will do what I can) or 前向きに検討します (I will consider it positively) may signal a polite non-commitment. 暗黙 (anmoku) means unspoken understanding.

配慮 (hairyō, consideration) towards the listener shapes word choice. The ウチ・ソト (in-group/out-group) distinction affects keigo. 曖昧 (aimai, vagueness) is sometimes strategic, to protect harmony. Irony (皮肉, hiniku) is understood from context, tone and relationship.

Care is needed: communication styles vary with the person, workplace, generation and region, so these are tendencies and not rules. Learners should notice patterns and verify meaning politely, for example by asking about timing or concrete steps.
sentences: Consideration for others appears in words.

gq.q: What might 前向きに検討します signal?
gq.why: It can be a polite non-commitment.

o: A kind of tea served at the door
A counter used for small things
gq.why: It is the in-group and out-group distinction.

panel.q: Why is it a mistake to say all Japanese speakers communicate indirectly?
panel.why: Styles vary with person, workplace, generation and region.

panel.q: How can a learner verify the meaning of 善処します?
panel.why: Ask politely about timing or concrete steps.

panel.q: Why might 曖昧 be strategic?
panel.why: Vagueness can protect harmony or save face.

teach.model: Japanese speakers may use indirect, softened expressions out of consideration for others. But styles vary, so these are tendencies. Check meaning politely by asking about timing or concrete steps.

trip.prompt: Find an example of indirect refusal in another language and compare.

stages.title: Language variation and dialectology
stages.hook: In Japan, the word for "snail" was said differently across the country. What can a map of dialect words tell us?
explain: Dialectology (方言学, hōgengaku) studies regional variation. The folklorist 柳田國男 (Yanagita Kunio) proposed the 方言周圏論 (hōgen shūkenron, dialect circles theory) in 蝸牛考 (1930): new words spread from a cultural centre in waves, so older forms survive in distant areas. The case study was words for "snail".

Pitch accent differs by region. The Tokyo-type accent (東京式) and the Kyoto–Osaka type (京阪式) are different systems, which is why the same word may have a different pitch pattern. Regional vocabulary also varies, such as おおきに in Kansai. Okinawan and other Ryukyuan languages differ from mainland dialects.

Language varies by generation (世代差, sedai-sa) too. Younger speakers use more standard forms, and "neo-dialects" mix standard and local speech. 役割語 (yakuwarigo, role language) is the use of speech styles for fictional characters, like "old man" speech; real people do not necessarily speak like this.
stages.mnemonic: Words travel from the centre; accents map the region.
sentences: Yanagita Kunio proposed the dialect circles theory.
Role language shows a character from the way of speaking.

gq.q: What does the dialect circles theory suggest?
o: Old forms survive in distant regions
gq.why: Older word forms may survive far from the centre.

o: A pitch accent system used in dialects of Kyoto
A particle that marks the speaker's role
A dictionary of fictional character names
Speech styles tied to character types
gq.why: It is language styles associated with fictional character types.

panel.q: Why might critics question simple dialect circles?
o: Because all words came from Tokyo
panel.why: Spread can also be affected by population movement and other factors, so the picture is more complex.

panel.q: Which statement about accent is accurate?
o: They are the same system with different names
Japanese has no accent, only pitch in writing
Accent is a feature of writing, not of speech
panel.why: Tokyo-type and Keihan-type are different pitch accent systems.

panel.q: What are neo-dialects?
o: Ancient dialects that disappeared long ago
A script used for writing local words
A mix of standard and local speech
A grammar term for new verb endings
panel.why: They mix standard and local speech among younger speakers.

teach.model: Dialectology maps regional variation. Yanagita proposed that new words spread from a centre, leaving old forms in distant places. Accent systems differ by region, and young speakers mix standard and local speech.

points.ask: What is the dialect circles theory?

trip.prompt: Look at a map of accent types in Japan and describe the two main areas.

stages.title: Specialised scientific or technical language
stages.hook: Many science words in Japanese were built from kanji in the 1800s. How do you make a new term for a new idea?
explain: Scientific Japanese often builds terms from kanji (和製漢語, wasei kango): 細胞 (saibō, cell), 電子 (denshi, electron), 情報 (jōhō, information), 半導体 (handōtai, semiconductor). In the Meiji period, scholars coined many such terms to translate Western knowledge. Some were later borrowed into Chinese and Korean.

Modern technical terms also use katakana loanwords such as ソフトウェア (software) and アルゴリズム (algorithm). Choice between kanji terms and katakana depends on the field. Standard lists (学術用語) guide experts. 人工知能 (jinkō chinō) is artificial intelligence.

Technical writing is precise: use である style, define terms (専門用語, senmon yōgo) at first use, keep one term per concept, and write units correctly. Long noun compounds are common, so the order of modifiers matters.
stages.mnemonic: New idea, kanji combination, standard term.
sentences: Semiconductors are used in electronic devices.

gq.why: 半導体 literally means half-conductor, a semiconductor.
It means kanji compounds coined in Japan.

panel.q: Why do technical documents keep one term per concept?
o: To save ink in printed manuals
To use more kanji in each text
To avoid verbs in technical sentences
panel.why: Using different terms could suggest different concepts.

panel.q: A Meiji scholar needs a Japanese word for a new Western idea. What was a common method?
o: Adopt romaji only and drop kanji
Ban the idea until it was understood
Combine kanji to coin a term
Wait for a natural tone change
panel.why: Scholars often combined kanji to create a term.

panel.q: When might a field prefer katakana?
panel.why: Katakana is often used for recent loanwords and new technology.

teach.model: Scientific Japanese builds terms from kanji, many coined in the Meiji period, and also uses katakana loanwords. Technical writing defines terms, uses one term per concept and keeps a precise style.

trip.prompt: Find three Meiji-era coined terms and see what they mean.

stages.title: Integrated proficiency project
stages.hook: You have studied kana, kanji, grammar and culture. How do you show what you can do and plan the next step?
explain: An integrated project (総合プロジェクト) combines reading, listening, speaking and writing around one topic, for example a presentation on a local issue with a summary, a short report and an interview. 発表 (happyō) is the presentation and 振り返り (furikaeri) is looking back.

The Japanese-Language Proficiency Test (日本語能力試験, JLPT) has five levels, N5 to N1, with N1 the most advanced. The test does not measure speaking directly. Approximate comparisons with CEFR levels exist but are not exact. A portfolio (ポートフォリオ) with recordings and writing samples shows real ability.

Self-assessment (自己評価, jiko hyōka) means setting goals (目標, mokuhyō), checking progress and planning practice. Typical weaknesses are keigo, kanji reading and listening speed. Plan daily listening, weekly writing and conversation with native speakers, and revisit your goals regularly.
sentences: My goal is to pass JLPT N2.
I reflect and make a plan.

gq.q: Which JLPT level is the most advanced?
What does 振り返り mean?
gq.why: It means reflecting on what you have done.

panel.q: Why is a portfolio useful?
o: It is only a test of kanji
It shows real work over time
It lists every kanji you know
panel.why: It shows real samples of ability over time.

panel.q: A learner has weak listening. What is a sensible plan?
o: Avoid listening and focus on kanji
panel.why: Targeted daily listening with feedback addresses the weakness.

panel.q: Why are CEFR comparisons with JLPT only approximate?
o: They are identical in design and scope
CEFR is a Japanese test of kanji
JLPT is a dictionary of grammar
panel.why: The tests were designed differently.

teach.model: A final project combines all four skills. The JLPT has five levels, N5 to N1. A portfolio shows real work, and self-assessment sets goals and plans next steps.

trip.prompt: Read about the JLPT levels and choose a realistic next goal.

sources: Common European Framework of Reference for Languages
